firmware.arch: LPC4370 Cortex-M4 (open firmware) + R820T2 / polyphase-HR front-end

notes: RX-only 12-bit (R2/Mini, 24-1800MHz) or high-DR HF/VHF (HF+ Discovery). Reference receive tier.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3 (NRC7292)

notes: First Wi-Fi HaLow Raspberry Pi HAT (~$70): Newracom NRC7292 + Qorvo RFFM6901 FEM. Host + standalone modes, up to 15 Mbps. The most practical hobbyist entry point for sub-GHz HaLow monitor/sniffer experiments via the open nrc7292_sw_pkg driver. Net-new named module record.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Zynq-7035 (ARM Cortex-A9 + 7-series FPGA) baseband in Verilog + Linux mac80211 driver

notes: Flagship 2x2 openwifi platform: ADI ADRV9361 SOM (Zynq-7035 + AD9361) on ADRV1CRR carrier. Fully open 802.11a/g/n PHY+MAC in FPGA; the true Tier-5 endpoint. Zynq-7035 requires a paid Vivado licence to rebuild the bitstream.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Zynq-7020 (ARM Cortex-A9 + 7-series FPGA) baseband in Verilog + Linux mac80211 driver

notes: Single-stream (1x1) openwifi platform: ADI ADRV9364 SOM (Zynq-7020 + AD9364). Cheapest ADI SOM entry; Zynq-7020 is covered by free Vivado WebPACK, so the FPGA can be rebuilt without a paid licence.

firmware.arch: Zynq-7010 dual Cortex-A9 + FPGA, AD9363 transceiver

notes: 325MHz-3.8GHz (hack: ~70MHz-6GHz via AD9364 re-ID), 12-bit, 20MHz BW, full-duplex 1x1. Go-to full-duplex transceiver for Wi-Fi-sensing researchers.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 microcode (custom 16-bit RISC), host-driven MAC, no on-die ARM

notes: SoftMAC 11g part with a fully open replacement microcode (OpenFWWF), compiled with b43-tools. Genuine open-firmware MAC (tier 5 by openness), but the 11g PHY offers no CSI/IQ path.

firmware.arch: D11 MAC microcode (core rev 5-14, no on-chip MAC CPU)

notes: Classic SoftMAC BCM43xx where the D11 ucode IS the entire MAC (no ARM co-processor). Because the driver loads the ucode as a plain file, OpenFWWF can replace it wholesale with fully open GPLv2 microcode built by b43-asm, making the card a programmable-MAC testbed. This is the reference platform for learning the D11 ISA from complete commented source rather than disassembly. firmware.openness=open reflects the OpenFWWF replacement; the PHY itself remains closed.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 microcode, host-driven MAC, no on-die ARM

notes: Primary chip OpenFWWF was tested on (4306 & 4318). Open MAC firmware; used to prototype custom MAC protocols. b43 gives native monitor+injection.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 microcode (proprietary), host-driven MAC

notes: Draft-11n MIMO SoftMAC part. Runs under b43 with proprietary ucode (not covered by OpenFWWF), so monitor/injection only.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 microcode (proprietary), host-driven MAC

notes: 2x2 11n dual-band SoftMAC. Native mac80211 monitor+injection; proprietary ucode (OpenFWWF never ported).

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 microcode (proprietary), host-driven MAC

notes: 2x2 2.4GHz 11n SoftMAC. b43 monitor+injection; proprietary ucode only.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M3

notes: Early combo FullMAC part. Historical Nexmon/RE interest; Cortex-M3. Limited modern tooling.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M3

notes: 1x1 dual-band 11n combo. Experimental Nexmon support; Cortex-M3.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M3

notes: 1x1 11n low-power combo. Experimental Nexmon; Cortex-M3.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-R4

notes: First-gen 1x1 11ac. Early Nexmon monitor/injection targets; Cortex-R4. Less maintained than 4339.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-R4-class + Broadcom D11 ucode

notes: Tier-4 evidence chip, re-anchored by the Tier-4 audit (docs/verification-tier4.md). The reproducible arbitrary-waveform proof is the MobiSys 2018 'Shadow Wi-Fi' nexmon SDR patch (FULL C source), not the WiSec 2017 jammer previously cited: three ioctls -- 426 NEX_WRITE_TEMPLATE_RAM, 427 START, 428 STOP -- write int16 I/Q into the D11 Template RAM and key the TX chain, emitting an arbitrary baseband buffer (not an 802.11 frame) in 2.4/5 GHz. TX-only; waveform length bounded by Template-RAM depth; band-limited, low-dynamic-range front-end. Monitor/injection/CSI are verified; arbitrary-TX stays 'reported' because the demonstrated target is a rooted Nexus 5 on stock fw 6.0.1 M4B30Z (EoL, hard to source) -- the same primitive on the Raspberry Pi bcm43455c0 is the practical path. The WiSec 2017 reactive jammer is an APPLICATION of this primitive but ships binary-only firmware deliberately restricted to NEXMON/JAMMER MACs, so it is not the reproducible route. Removed the prior 'raw-iq' flag: nexmon exposes frequency-domain CSI, not time-domain IQ receive.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M3 (ROM at ~0x800000)

notes: Single-stream 2.4GHz-only 11n (Pi 3B / Zero W). Nexmon monitor+injection verified (fw 7_45_41_46). Cortex-M3, ROM at upper address. Not in the official nexmon_csi list.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M3

notes: The silicon in the Pi Zero 2 W. Nexmon monitor+injection verified (fw 9_88_4_65). 2.4GHz single-stream 11n, Cortex-M3.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3 (host firmware) + D11 MAC microcode (PSM)

notes: Single-stream 802.11n FullMAC SoC in the Pi Zero W and early Pi 3. Classic target for D11 ucode disassembly: its ucode is stored 7-byte-packed inside the ARM RAM firmware and unpacked by the ARM before being loaded into the D11 core; b43-tools PR#4 reproduces the packing so the ucode can be round-tripped through b43-dasm/b43-asm. Nexmon provides monitor mode and frame injection; CSI export is not officially supported on this part (reported/experimental only).

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-R/M-class + Broadcom D11 ucode

notes: Corrected UPWARD Tier 3 -> 4 by the Tier-4 audit (docs/verification-tier4.md). The MobiSys 2018 'Shadow Wi-Fi' nexmon SDR patch explicitly supports the bcm43455c0 on a Raspberry Pi 3B+ (NOT the plain 3B) with FULL public source, giving the same arbitrary-IQ TX primitive as the Nexus-5 bcm4339 (ioctls 426/427/428 write int16 I/Q to Template RAM). This makes the Pi the most reproducible Tier-4 Wi-Fi target in the catalog -- current, cheap hardware. Monitor/injection/CSI(80MHz, int16)/spectral remain independently VERIFIED; the arbitrary-waveform rung is 'reported' (research patch, not a turnkey nexutil feature; firmware version string e.g. 7_45_189/206 must match the shipped blob). TX-only; band-limited, low dynamic range. status is set to 'reported' to track the tier-defining capability per the taxonomy convention while the lower rungs stay verified.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 ucode + ARM Cortex-R/M

sdr_tier_rationale: Per-subcarrier CSI up to 80 MHz (up to 4x4 on RT-AC86U) via Nexmon firmware patch; delivered as UDP/pcap.
notes: The canonical firmware-RE CSI path; runs on cheap Pis, phones, routers. See ../chips/broadcom-cypress.md and ../projects/nexmon.md.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-R4

notes: 2x2 11ac in the Nexus 6 (distinct from 4358 in Nexus 6P). Nexmon injection reported; CSI porting plausible given Cortex-R4 sibling status to 4358.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-R4

notes: 2x2 11ac (Nexus 6P). Nexmon monitor/inject (fw 7_112_201_3_sta) and nexmon_csi (fw 7_112_300_14_sta, 80MHz, 2 streams) verified. Cortex-R4. Distinct from BCM4356 in Nexus 6.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-R4

notes: 2x2 11ac. Community nexmon monitor/injection patches exist; CSI ports attempted. Cortex-R4.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM

notes: 2x2 11ac part sometimes paired with 802.11ad radios. No public Nexmon port; listed for completeness and future RE.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 MAC ucode + on-chip ARM (fullmac)
re_tooling: nexmon (no published port for this chip)

notes: Ubiquitous 3x3 802.11ac Broadcom radio in the most-recommended AC-era routers and many Macs. Despite that popularity it is NOT a public SDR target: BCM4360 is absent from Nexmon's supported firmwares and is not a nexmon_csi chip, so out of the box you get station-mode only (tier 0 black box). It is a Broadcom D11-family part, so a Nexmon port is theoretically possible but none is published. Cataloged specifically to correct the common myth that a Netgear R7000/R8000 can do Wi-Fi CSI - buy an ASUS RT-AC86U (BCM4366c0) for CSI or a Netgear R7800 (QCA9984) for spectral instead.

firmware.arch: ARM + Broadcom D11 ucode

notes: Router-class 4x4 MIMO CSI at 80 MHz via nexmon_csi (firmware 10_10_122_20). Float-style CSI encoding (sign/exponent/mantissa) rather than the int16 format used by bcm4339/bcm43455c0.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM Cortex-M7

notes: 2x2 Wi-Fi 6 (Galaxy S10/S20). Nexmon monitor+injection verified (S20 fw 18_41_8_9_sta) on rooted, SELinux-permissive devices; CSI ported by community. Newer Cortex-M7-class core.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + ARM (Apple-customized firmware, PCIe)

notes: Apple's customized Broadcom Wi-Fi 6. Same D11+ARM lineage but locked-down, PCIe-attached, Apple firmware signing — no public Nexmon monitor/inject. Reverse-engineering only (e.g. via Asahi/brcmfmac efforts).

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 PHY microcode + dual ARM Cortex-M-class cores

notes: 2x2 Wi-Fi 6E (Pixel 7). Nexmon monitor+injection verified (fw 20_101_57) on Magisk-rooted devices. 6GHz-capable. CSI not yet upstream.

firmware.arch: ARM firmware + D11 ucode (Nexmon-patchable)

notes: Broadcom's 11be mobile combo (2x2 SDB, 320 MHz, 5-7 GHz, 4K-QAM, dual-core BT 5.2). Nexmon lists BCM4398d05,8,9 (fw 24_671_6_9) on a rooted Pixel 8 with Monitor Mode + RadioTap enabled; frame injection is NOT listed for this part, and nexmon_csi does NOT support any Wi-Fi 7 chip. Firmware is patchable via the Nexmon toolchain (same D11/ARM model as older BCM43xx) but no 11be CSI patch has been published.

firmware.arch: Broadcom proprietary AP SDK firmware

common_hardware: Wi-Fi 6/6E router and AP reference designs
notes: Wi-Fi 6/6E access-point SoC on Broadcom's closed router SDK. No Nexmon foothold and no open driver; effectively black-box for SDR-style repurposing. Listed for completeness alongside BCM4398; for an open 6E AP for sensing, prefer an MT7916-class MediaTek AP instead.

firmware.arch: Celeno proprietary Wi-Fi + Doppler engine

notes: Built-in Wi-Fi Doppler radar mode (WFD) detects presence, falls, gestures, even breathing through walls in 5/6 GHz. The purest Wi-Fi-as-radar product in the catalog, but the Doppler engine is a closed proprietary feature with no public API, firmware, or RE tooling: tier 2 by capability but locked.

firmware.arch: Broadcom/Cypress D11 microcode + ARM Cortex-M3 (low-power)

notes: Ultra-low-power 1x1 combo aimed at wearables/IoT. Cypress/Infineon SDK gives partial documentation; no confirmed Nexmon monitor/CSI. Candidate for future porting.

firmware.arch: Cypress D11 microcode + ARM (USB-attached)

notes: 1x1 11ac USB combo driven by brcmfmac. Same D11+ARM family; monitor/injection plausible via a Nexmon port but unproven. Attractive because USB-attached and cheap.

firmware.arch: Cypress D11 microcode + ARM (automotive-qualified)

notes: Automotive-grade 2x2 11ac with 802.11p (DSRC/V2X). Same lineage; no public RE. Cataloged for future 802.11p-repurposing interest.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa LX6 (dual-core, 240 MHz)

notes: The reference CSI platform: built-in esp_wifi_set_csi_config/esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb yields per-subcarrier complex CSI (up to 52-64 usable subcarriers HT20). Raw TX via esp_wifi_80211_tx, promiscuous RX with rx_ctrl (RSSI/noise/rate/timestamp). No FFT/spectral or IQ API -> hard tier-2 ceiling. Wi-Fi MAC/PHY shipped as closed libpp/libnet80211/libphy blobs.

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V single-core (120 MHz)

notes: Cost-optimized, thin RAM/flash. Monitor + raw TX verified. CSI is limited/unverified: the C2 is notably absent from Espressif's canonical CSI-support enumeration (ESP32/S2/C3/S3/C5/C6/C61). Treat CSI as reported at best on this SKU.

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V single-core (RV32IMC, 160 MHz)

notes: First RISC-V Espressif Wi-Fi part; cheapest reliable CSI node. Full CSI/monitor/raw-TX support. Open RV32 core toolchain, closed Wi-Fi PHY blob (same tier-2 ceiling).

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V single-core (240 MHz)

notes: Espressif's first dual-band 2.4+5 GHz Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) part. CSI supported on BOTH bands per Espressif's support list -> the accessible route to 5 GHz CSI without a Broadcom/Intel firmware jailbreak, a genuinely new hobbyist capability. Wi-Fi 6 HE-LTF CSI is newer; expect the same maturing-quirk risk as the C6.

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V HP core (160 MHz) + LP core; RV32IMAC

notes: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) + BLE 5 + 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee/Matter). CSI/monitor/TX supported. HE CSI has documented rough edges: IDF #14271 reports missing L-LTF data and wrong HT-LTF subcarrier ordering in the callback. HT (11n) CSI is solid; HE CSI is evolving.

firmware.arch: Xtensa LX6/LX7 (ESP32/S-series) or RISC-V (C-series); Wi-Fi MAC closed blob, CSI via public API

sdr_tier_rationale: Native ESP-IDF wifi_csi_info_t exposes up to 52/64 subcarriers (L-LTF/HT-LTF), 1x1; no firmware reversing needed.
notes: Only Tier-2 path with an official vendor CSI API. C6 adds Wi-Fi 6 but has known LTF ordering quirks (esp-idf #14271). See ../chips/espressif.md.

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V single-core (96 MHz)

notes: NO Wi-Fi radio -> no Wi-Fi CSI, out of the core Wi-Fi-SDR thesis. Included for completeness: it offers raw 802.15.4 frame RX/TX at 2.4 GHz (a different-standard analog of monitor/injection) plus BLE 5. Catalogued at the floor for Wi-Fi purposes.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa LX7 (single-core, 240 MHz)

notes: Wi-Fi only (no Bluetooth). Full CSI/monitor/raw-TX API parity with ESP32. Native USB-OTG makes it a clean USB-tethered CSI capture dongle.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa LX7 (dual-core + vector/SIMD DSP, 240 MHz)

notes: Same CSI/monitor/TX APIs as ESP32; the LX7 vector extensions make on-device CSI feature extraction and TinyML sensing (motion/respiration classifiers) viable without offloading.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa L106 (single-core, 80/160 MHz)

notes: Monitor + injection are the classic, verified use (deauth/sniffer platform). CSI is documented in Espressif's ESP-FAQ via esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb() but the mainstream CSI toolkits (ESP32-CSI-Tool, Wi-ESP) are all ESP32; ESP8266 CSI is reported, not community-proven. No spectral/IQ access. Wi-Fi PHY is a closed blob.

firmware.arch: AD936x/AD9371 transceiver + Spartan/Kintex/Zynq FPGA (open UHD, large FPGA on N310)

notes: Research-standard. B200/B210 70MHz-6GHz 56MHz BW 12-bit; N310 4x4 10MHz-6GHz up to 100MHz/ch 14-bit. Far end of the yardstick; instrument-grade open PHY.

re_tooling: Morse Micro GPL-2.0 mac80211 driver / OpenWrt SDK

notes: M.2 HaLow radio card built on Morse Micro MM8108 (second-gen). Targets embedded gateways/SBCs. Inherits Morse open GPL mac80211 driver (tier-1 monitor+injection) and closed MM8108 firmware blob + BCF. Net-new named module record; complements the earlier NRC7292-based Gateworks GW16146 mini-PCIe.

firmware.arch: NXP LPC43xx Cortex-M4/M0 (open firmware)

notes: 1MHz-6GHz, 20MHz BW, 8-bit, half-duplex TX/RX. Canonical open TX-capable hacker SDR; the arbitrary-waveform reference.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3 (NXP LPC1756) + CC2400 transceiver

notes: Open 2.4 GHz platform: CC2400 transceiver + LPC1756 Cortex-M3, fully open firmware (bluetooth_rxtx). Sniffs BLE, partial BT Classic (BR), and runs ubertooth-specan, a real spectrum-analyzer/spectral-scan across 2.4 GHz via CC2400 RSSI sweeps (tier 3). Because the firmware is yours, the CC2400's PHY telemetry is fully exposed.

firmware.arch: 8051 core + CC1101-class radio + USB

notes: CC1111 = CC1101 radio + 8051 + USB. YARD Stick One runs RfCat (open firmware) exposing the transceiver from an interactive Python shell: 2-FSK/GFSK/MSK/ASK/OOK, raw register access, RSSI-sweep spectrum. RfCat also supports CC1110/CC2510/CC2511.

firmware.arch: 60 GHz radar MMIC + integrated FSM/FIFO; host MCU control (Avian driver)

notes: PURPOSE-BUILT radar included as the yardstick, NOT a repurposed Wi-Fi chip. The 60 GHz FMCW radar behind Google Soli (Pixel 4 gesture control, Nest presence/sleep sensing). 57-64 GHz, >5 GHz sweep bandwidth, 1 Tx / 3 Rx antenna-in-package (L-shaped for azimuth+elevation). Configured via Infineon's documented Radar SDK / Avian driver / Fusion GUI, which expose raw IQ frames -> range-Doppler-angle. Tier 4 (arbitrary FMCW chirp + raw IQ). Canonical reference for what a real 60 GHz gesture/vital-sign radar looks like when benchmarking a Wi-Fi-based imitation.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware (signed); iwlwifi-cc-a0 ucode

notes: Wi-Fi 6 (11ax) 2x2. First post-5300 Intel CSI, via AX-CSI (research), FeitCSI (turn-key, MIT, GUI/CLI, also frame injection) and PicoScenes (multi-NIC, up to 27 concurrent). CSI for all OFDM formats 11a/g/n/ac/ax; AX-CSI handles up to 160 MHz HE / ~1992 subcarriers per packet; FeitCSI up to 512 subcarriers at 16-bit signed. Firmware is closed/signed - tools ride the vendor's own CSI/debug host-command surface. Ceiling tier 2 (frame-level injection does not raise the tier).

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware (signed); iwlwifi-ty-a0 ucode

notes: Wi-Fi 6E: adds the 6 GHz band (5945-7125 MHz) and 160 MHz channels. Intel's most capable sensing NIC today. PicoScenes is (per its authors) the first/only public platform doing 11ax CSI + packet injection in 6 GHz on the AX210; FeitCSI also captures 6 GHz CSI. Same closed/signed firmware model as AX200. Ceiling tier 2.

firmware.arch: Intel closed microcode (ARC-based), iwlwifi

sdr_tier_rationale: CSI for all 802.11a/g/n/ac/ax formats up to 160 MHz (up to ~1992 subcarriers/packet), 6 GHz on AX210, via patched microcode; FeitCSI adds injection + GUI.
notes: Modern Wi-Fi 6/6E CSI. AX-CSI (WiNTECH'21) first; FeitCSI is the packaged CLI+GUI+live-USB; PicoScenes is the multi-NIC platform. See ../chips/intel.md.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware (signed); iwlwifi-gl ucode

notes: Intel's first Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) part: 2x2, 2.4/5/6 GHz, up to 320 MHz and 4K-QAM. No published tool yet confirms 320 MHz 11be CSI; FeitCSI authors note only 'high possibility' the newest NIC is supported, and AX-CSI/PicoScenes docs stop at AX210/AX211. Treat CSI as emerging/reported until a verified capture appears. Firmware closed/signed.

firmware.arch: Intel closed ucode (gl series) + PNVM platform blob

common_hardware: CNVio2 soldered-down module (requires Intel host MAC)
notes: CNVio2 companion of BE200; same 'Gale' (gl) firmware family. Upstream iwlwifi monitor works from kernel 6.5; injection is firmware-restricted as on all Intel parts. CSI is NOT available: PicoScenes/FeitCSI verify only AX200/AX210, and the AX210 firmware-notification RE has not been ported to the Gale blob. For commodity Intel CSI today use AX210, not a BE200/BE201.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel Wireless-MAC microcontroller; iwlwifi-4965 ucode

notes: Intel's first 802.11n (draft-n) part, 2x3 MIMO. No CSI/PHY telemetry path; monitor/injection only via mac80211/iwl4965.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel Wireless-MAC microcontroller; iwlwifi-5000 ucode

notes: Lower-antenna siblings of the 5300. The 5300 CSI ucode hard-codes 3 receive chains, so the 1x2 5100 / 2x2 5150 are NOT supported by the CSI tool. Usable only as ordinary mac80211 monitor/injection radios.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel Wireless-MAC microcontroller (undocumented ISA); iwlwifi-5000 ucode

common_hardware: Intel WiFi Link 5300 mini-PCIe card (3 antennas required)
notes: The original 802.11n CSI tool. Reports channel matrix H for 30 subcarrier groups, signed 8-bit I and 8-bit Q per Tx/Rx pair (up to 3x3), plus per-chain RSSI/noise/AGC. Requires the patched 'connector' ucode + patched iwlwifi/mac80211, pinned to old kernels (classic: Ubuntu 10.04 / 2.6.36). Only the 3-antenna 5300 works; 5100/5150 excluded by hard-coded 3-chain layout. Ceiling is tier 2 (CSI) - no spectral/raw-IQ/arbitrary-TX.

firmware.arch: Intel closed microcode (iwlwifi)

sdr_tier_rationale: Grouped 30-subcarrier CSI (int8 real/imag), up to 3x3, via patched microcode + modified iwlwifi.
notes: The original commodity CSI tool (SIGCOMM CCR 2011). 30 subcarrier groups, 20/40 MHz 802.11n. Kernel/firmware-version locked. See ../chips/intel.md.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel Wireless-MAC microcontroller; iwlwifi-6000 ucode

notes: The 6300 is a 3x3 802.11n part sometimes floated as a 5300 stand-in, but no maintained public CSI firmware exists for the 6000 series. Monitor/injection only.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware split; iwlwifi-7260/7265 ucode

notes: First 802.11ac Intel generation, 2x2. No public CSI/PHY tooling; monitor/injection only. Firmware moves to the signed LMAC/UMAC image model.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware; iwlwifi-8000C/8265 ucode (signed)

notes: 802.11ac 2x2. No public CSI path; monitor/injection only. Firmware is signed.

firmware.arch: Proprietary Intel LMAC + UMAC firmware; iwlwifi-9000 ucode (signed)

notes: 802.11ac Wave 2, 2x2. 9260 is discrete; 9560 is CNVi (companion RF next to the CPU). No maintained public CSI tooling. Monitor/injection only.

firmware.arch: LMS7002M field-programmable RF + FX3/FPGA

notes: 100kHz-3.8GHz (Mini 10MHz-3.5GHz), 12-bit, up to 61.44/30.72 MSPS, 2x2 / 1x1 full-duplex. Favored for open-source cellular.

firmware.arch: ThreadX RTOS on on-chip MAC/PHY controller

key_projects.name: Project Zero: Over The Air (Marvell Avastar firmware RE)

notes: mwifiex gives monitor mode (tier 1). Gal Beniamini reverse-engineered the 88W8897 Wi-Fi firmware (ThreadX RTOS) for exploitation, proving the firmware is openable with IDA/Ghidra, but no SDR/CSI feature has been productized, so CSI is only reported.

firmware.arch: MediaTek on-chip MCU (ROM patch + RAM firmware)

sdr_notes: 802.11b/g/n 1T1R 2.4 GHz, in kernel since 4.2. Monitor mode works; INJECTION is limited/unreliable in practice (widely reported). Treat as Tier 1 with caveat.
notes: Open mt7601u driver, closed MCU firmware. Cheapest MediaTek dongle; monitor good, injection flaky.

firmware.arch: MediaTek on-chip MCU (ROM patch + RAM firmware)

sdr_notes: 802.11ac 1T1R dual-band; adds 5 GHz monitor+injection in a tiny package via mt76x0u. Tier 1.
notes: Open mt76 driver, closed MCU firmware.

firmware.arch: MediaTek on-chip MCU (ROM patch + RAM firmware)

sdr_notes: 802.11ac 2T2R dual-band ~866 Mbit/s; the chip in the Alfa AWUS036ACM. The MODERN reference monitor+injection dongle on stock in-tree mt76x2u (since kernel 4.19) — clean injection both bands. Tier 1.
notes: Distinct from AWUS036AC (RTL8812AU). Open mt76 driver, closed MCU firmware. PCIe sibling MT7612E is the same PHY.

firmware.arch: ConnAC dual-MCU: WM (WiFi-MAC) + WA (WiFi-Algorithm) firmware, ARM-class cores

sdr_notes: 802.11ac 4x4 DBDC AP/router (MT7615) and 2x2 client (MT7663). Introduces the ConnAC dual-MCU (WM+WA) design. Monitor+injection verified (Tier 1). CSI hooks far less mature than the Wi-Fi 6 family — experimental/reported.
notes: Open mt76 driver, closed WM/WA blobs but open MCU-command interface. Unlock path is driver patching, not firmware patching.

firmware.arch: MediaTek closed on-chip firmware blob; open mt76 driver

notes: Wi-Fi 6E (not Wi-Fi 7, despite the similar name to MT7925/7927). Upstream mt76 support was added 'based on MT7921', so it reuses the mature mt7921 code path with monitor and injection. CSI via MtkCSIdump is plausible (same mt76 family) but unverified on this specific part.

firmware.arch: ConnAC2 dual-MCU: WM (WiFi-MAC) + WA (WiFi-Algorithm) firmware, ARM-class cores; ROM patch + RAM code

common_hardware: GL.iNet / Xiaomi / TP-Link Archer OpenWrt routers
sdr_notes: THE MediaTek Tier-2 platform. 802.11ax up to 4x4/160 MHz. Per-subcarrier CSI (amplitude + phase, up to ~512 subcarriers) exported via an nl80211 vendor command in patched mt76 — NO firmware modification needed; the closed MCU already computes CSI and the open driver taps the report. MtkCSIdump provides the patch+userland; ekstra-csi preserves MAC/RSSI/SNR metadata.
notes: Cheapest/cleanest Wi-Fi-6 CSI route on commodity routers. Dual-MCU WM+WA; unlock is a DRIVER patch, unlike Broadcom's nexmon firmware patch. See ../projects/csi-toolchains.md.

firmware.arch: ConnAC2 dual-MCU: WM + WA firmware, ARM-class cores

sdr_notes: 802.11ax 2x2 client (M.2/USB/SDIO). Monitor verified; injection present but historically buggy in 11ax framing (tracked in morrownr/USB-WiFi). CSI on the client MCU is not yet a turnkey public tool — theoretical/reported. Tier 1.
notes: In the Alfa AWUS036AXM. Shares ConnAC MCU-command lineage with MT7915, so client-side CSI is a plausible next target.

firmware.arch: ConnAC2 dual-MCU: WM + WA firmware, ARM-class cores

sdr_notes: 802.11ax Wi-Fi 6E 2x2 client; adds 6 GHz. Driven by the mt7921 sub-driver. Monitor+injection verified (same caveats as MT7921). CSI reported/theoretical. Tier 1.
notes: In the Alfa AWUS036AXML. 6 GHz-capable client on open mt76.

firmware.arch: ConnAC3 dual/triple-MCU firmware, ARM-class cores

sdr_notes: Newest Wi-Fi 7 clients covered by mt76 (mt7925). Monitor/injection maturing; CSI unexplored publicly. Tier 1, status reported pending more testing.
notes: Natural next-cycle target: whether the MT7915-style vendor-CSI path extends to Wi-Fi 7 client MCUs.

firmware.arch: MediaTek closed on-chip firmware blob; open mt76 driver

notes: 2x2 11be client, 320 MHz, 4K-QAM, MLO; architecturally an MT7925 Wi-Fi die (+MT6639 BT) on PCIe, so it rides the open mt76/mt7925 driver which supports STA/AP/P2P/monitor and good injection. Upstreaming was in ~4th review round on linux-wireless (2025-2026); out-of-tree DKMS covers kernels 6.17+. CSI NOT yet available on 11be: MtkCSIdump works on older MT7915/MT7921 without firmware mods but has not been ported to 320 MHz 11be — the most tractable open CSI target here given the open driver.

firmware.arch: ConnAC3 triple-core: WM + WA + WO (WiFi-offload) MCU firmware; ROM patch + RAM code

sdr_notes: Filogic router SoC where MediaTek CSI extraction was actually demonstrated: OpenWrt One (MT7981B, mt7976 radio) under OpenWrt 24.10 with MtkCSIdump patches. 802.11ax CSI via mt76 vendor dump, no firmware mod. Tier 2.
notes: The concrete, reproducible MediaTek CSI target as of 2024-2026. Triple-MCU (WM/WA/WO). Firmware blobs shipped in linux-firmware/mediatek.

firmware.arch: Ralink proprietary MAC microcode (small MCU)

sdr_notes: Earliest Ralink generation. Solid monitor+injection via open rt2x00/rt2500pci/rt73usb, but 802.11b/g 2.4 GHz only; obsolete. No CSI/spectral path.
notes: Canonical early aircrack-ng cards. Open driver, closed MAC microcode blob. Never climbed past Tier 1.

firmware.arch: Ralink proprietary MAC microcode (rt2870.bin/rt3070.bin, small MCU)

sdr_notes: THE classic USB injection chipset for a decade. 802.11n 1T1R/2T2R 2.4 GHz, SoftMAC → monitor+injection just work under rt2800usb.
notes: Reference cheap injection dongle. Open driver, closed MAC microcode. Tier 1 only.

firmware.arch: Ralink proprietary MAC microcode (small MCU)

sdr_notes: Added dual-band (2.4/5 GHz) monitor+injection in the Ralink era; valued for 5 GHz work before mt76 parts existed.
notes: rt2800usb dual-band 802.11n. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: Ralink proprietary MAC microcode (small MCU)

sdr_notes: Low-power 1T1R (RT5370) / 2T2R (RT5372) 2.4 GHz 802.11n; good injection, extremely common. Tier 1.
notes: Late-Ralink low-power parts, rt2800usb. No CSI/spectral.

firmware.arch: fixed-function 802.15.4 transceiver; ATmega128RFA1 adds an AVR core

notes: IEEE 802.15.4 transceivers (2.4 GHz and sub-GHz) plus the ATmega128RFA1/256RFR2 AVR radio SoCs. KillerBee drives the RZUSBstick and RZ Raven for monitor + injection. Documented PHYs; RIOT/Contiki drive them bare-metal.

firmware.arch: dual independent transceiver + baseband, with a documented raw I/Q LVDS interface that bypasses the baseband

notes: The accidental true-ish SDR of the non-Wi-Fi set: a documented raw I/Q data interface (three LVDS lanes, 13-bit I/Q up to ~4 MHz) lets you bypass the on-chip baseband, pull raw complex samples for your own DSP, and feed arbitrary I/Q in for TX. That is tier-4 arbitrary-waveform/raw-iq access with no firmware reversing, because the port is manufacturer-documented. Narrowband, but genuine front-end-level access on a commodity ISM chip.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Zynq-7020 (ARM Cortex-A9 + 7-series FPGA) baseband in Verilog + Linux mac80211 driver

notes: PlutoSDR-form-factor, low-cost openwifi target: MicroPhase ANTSDR family (E310v2, E200) = Zynq-7020 + AD9361/AD9363. openwifi provides prebuilt images; the closest 'Pluto-adjacent' way to run the full open 802.11 stack (the ADALM-Pluto's own Zynq-7010 is too small for the full PL).

firmware.arch: Morse Micro proprietary radio+PHY+MAC SoC

key_projects.name: Morse Micro chips (open mac80211 morse driver)

notes: Sub-1 GHz OFDM Wi-Fi (802.11ah), 1/2/4/8 MHz channels. Open mac80211 morse driver (upstreaming) enables monitor + injection at sub-GHz where wall penetration favors sensing. Firmware is a closed blob; no CSI toolchain yet but HaLow CSI is an active research direction.

re_tooling: GPL-2.0 mac80211 host driver (Morse Micro GitHub)

notes: Second-gen Morse Micro HaLow SoC (CES 2025). World-first sub-GHz 256-QAM at 8 MHz, up to 43.33 Mbps; 5x5mm BGA; adds USB 2.0 host + MIPI RFFE alongside SDIO/SPI; integrated PA/LNA; 850-950 MHz. Host driver is open GPL mac80211 (monitor+injection reachable); radio PHY/MAC firmware is a closed binary blob with board-config (BCF) files and no public RE toolchain. No public CSI/spectral export.

firmware.arch: Synopsys ARC (ARCompact) WiGig firmware; ARM host SoC

notes: QCA9500 (VIVE) single-stream 60 GHz radio on a beefier ARM host SoC. Same wil6210/ARC firmware internals as the Talon, but without an equally mature open LEDE/OpenWrt image exposing the WiGig debugfs, so firmware patching is less turnkey than the Talon. Used in localization/gesture/'beyond-RF' beamforming sensing papers. Tier 2 by the same beam-SNR argument as the Talon; status 'reported' because the patched-firmware sensing path is less broadly reproduced on this box than on the AD7200.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3

notes: First commercial 802.11ah HaLow SoC. ARM Cortex-M3, 752KB SRAM, no on-chip flash; host mode (CSPI/SDIO/UART/USB) or standalone. Unusually open host stack: GPL-2.0 mac80211 driver (nrc7292_sw_pkg) with explicit sniffer/monitor mode + radiotap, so tier-1 monitor+injection is verified today. Requires patched kernel/hostap/wireless-regdb for S1G channelization (not mainlined). PHY/MAC firmware (uni_s1g.bin) is a closed blob; no public CSI or firmware RE path. Already referenced as morsemicro-mm6108's counterpart; net-new full record here.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3

notes: Cost/power-optimized second-gen Newracom HaLow SoC (2023). Baseband (MAC+PHY) + sub-1GHz transceiver + ADC/DAC + integrated PA (up to +17 dBm) in 6x6mm 48-QFN; 1/2/4 MHz channels, 750-950 MHz; ARM Cortex-M3 standalone-capable. Same GPL-2.0 nrc7292_sw_pkg driver family covers 7292/7393/7394, so tier-1 monitor+injection carries over. Firmware closed; no CSI/spectral export.

firmware.arch: fixed-function 2.4 GHz GFSK transceiver (no MCU); nRF24LU1+ adds an 8051

key_projects.name: Goodspeed: Promiscuity is the nRF24L01+'s Duty

notes: Travis Goodspeed's pseudo-promiscuous trick (2-byte address, no CRC, preamble-as-MAC) turns this stock transceiver into a sniffer for compatible 2.4 GHz ShockBurst traffic. Underpins Bastille's MouseJack running nrf-research-firmware on the Crazyradio PA. Documented PHY, no firmware to reverse.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M0 (nRF51) / Cortex-M4F (nRF52) / Cortex-M33 (nRF53/nRF54)

notes: Nordic fully documents the RADIO peripheral at register level (openness=documented, not closed), so bare-metal code and the official radio_test sample configure BLE 1M/2M/Coded, 802.15.4, or proprietary GFSK, plus carrier/tone TX and promiscuous RX. Platform under Sniffle, nRF Sniffer, and a large tool ecosystem. Tier 1 with enough raw-RADIO control to shape arbitrary GFSK packets.

firmware.arch: AD9361 transceiver + Cyclone V FPGA (49k/301k LE) + ARM Cortex-M4

notes: 47MHz-6GHz, up to 56MHz BW, 12-bit, 2x2 MIMO full-duplex, USB 3.0. xA4/xA9 differ only in FPGA size (on-board user DSP/PHY).

firmware.arch: fixed-function UWB transceiver with SPI-readable CIR accumulator (no MCU)

key_projects.name: UWB CIR for device-free localization (MDPI Sensors)

notes: Ultra-wideband (~500 MHz channels, 3.5-6.5 GHz). The CIR accumulator exposes the full complex channel impulse response, up to 1016 taps of 16-bit I + 16-bit Q at ~1 ns spacing, directly over SPI: a UWB analog of CSI with amplitude and phase. Basis for a large body of device-free localization, occupancy, and radar-style sensing research. Tier 2 reaching toward tier 3. Fully documented, no firmware to reverse.

firmware.arch: on-chip Tensilica/ARM, closed firmware blob (ath10k/pci or snoc)

sdr_reason: Mobile 11ac combo on ath10k. Monitor mode works but injection and PHY telemetry are gated by the closed firmware; spectral is not reliably exposed on this SKU. Practically Tier 1.
notes: Ubiquitous laptop Wi-Fi. The WCN3990 is the closely related integrated-in-SoC phone variant.

firmware.arch: on-chip Tensilica/ARM, closed firmware blob loaded by ath11k

sdr_reason: Wi-Fi 6/6E on ath11k. Monitor mode works; ath11k carries a spectral path for some parts but end-to-end FFT dumps on these mobile SKUs are not turnkey — reported, not verified. CSI is research-stage. Practically Tier 1.
notes: WCN685x = FastConnect 6800/6900 (6E). QCA6390 firmware < a certain version had host-memory-below-32MB bugs. spectral-scan flag is aspirational for these parts.

firmware.arch: integrated mobile combo, closed firmware

sdr_reason: Mobile Wi-Fi 6E combo; fully closed firmware and integrated into phone platforms. Any PHY-telemetry unlock would require reversing the closed firmware — theoretical today.
notes: Included to mark the current mobile frontier for the next cycle. See ../docs/firmware-reversing.md.

firmware.arch: ARC (Argonaut RISC Core) microcode

key_projects.name: Channel estimation & custom beamforming on Talon AD7200

notes: 60 GHz single-stream over a 32-element phased array with analog beamforming. SEEMOO's nexmon-arc ports Nexmon to the chip's ARC microcode (on ported LEDE), enabling per-sector channel estimation (CSI) and authoring of arbitrary custom beam patterns loaded into the array: tier 2 telemetry shading into tier 3/4 programmable spatial front-end. Substrate for commodity 60 GHz mmWave sensing/imaging research.

firmware.arch: Qualcomm closed firmware + board-2.bin (ath12k)

common_hardware: M.2 E-key AP radio modules (e.g. Wallys DR9274)
notes: AP-class 11be radios: QCN9274 is 4x4 MU-MIMO tri-band, QCN6274 a power-optimized fewer-stream variant, both 320 MHz. Same ath12k stack as WCN7850. ath11k on prior-gen QCN parts exposed a spectral-scan (FFT) debugfs; that capability is not yet present in ath12k, so spectral/raw-PHY is unreachable today. No CSI or injection tooling.

firmware.arch: integrated mobile radio, closed firmware (ath10k snoc/WCN)

sdr_reason: Integrated phone Wi-Fi driven by ath10k over the snoc bus; closed firmware limits it to monitor-class use. No public CSI/spectral path.
notes: The QCA6174-class radio integrated into Snapdragon platforms. Catalogued to mark the mobile frontier.

firmware.arch: Qualcomm closed firmware + board-2.bin (ath12k/WCN7850)

notes: 2x2 tri-band 11be client, 320 MHz, 4K-QAM, MLO. Driven by upstream ath12k (forked from ath11k) over PCIe; needs Qualcomm firmware + board-2.bin. Monitor mode was absent for ~2 years and merged through 2025 (adds RX monitor SRNG rings + IRQ config). No public injection, no CSI tool, and the ath11k spectral-scan FFT interface has NOT been forwarded to ath12k. Firmware closed; no Nexmon-equivalent.

firmware.arch: Synopsys ARC (ARCompact)

notes: Wilocity 'Sparrow' 60 GHz 802.11ad chipset: QCA6320 MAC/baseband + QCA6310 RF, driven by the mainline wil6210 driver with FullMAC firmware on ARC cores. SEEMOO's nexmon-arc patches wil6210 fw v4.1.0.55 / v5.2.0.18 to expose a 'sweep_dump' debugfs table of per-sector-sweep signal strength (beam-SNR). Beam-SNR is magnitude-only beam-space power, not per-subcarrier CSI, so we flag 'radar'/monitor/injection but deliberately NOT 'csi'. Tier 2: exports a spatial channel-state measurement usable as an angle-resolved pseudo-radar.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC, MAC/PHY driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: First Atheros 802.11n MAC/baseband; open SoftMAC gives full monitor + arbitrary frame injection but predates the AR92xx spectral-scan register interface, so no FFT/CSI path.
notes: AR5416 + AR5133 radio = the AR5008 chipset. The ath5k driver handles the earlier 11a/b/g AR52xx/AR54xx parts (also Tier 1). No on-chip firmware to reverse.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa (Magpie / K2 platforms), eCos RTOS

sdr_reason: The one part in the family with real on-chip firmware — and Qualcomm released the full Xtensa source. Patchable firmware enables reactive jamming, timing-controlled and raw injection (modwifi), while ath9k_htc spectral scan (ATH9K_HTC_DEBUGFS + ATH9K_COMMON_SPECTRAL) gives Tier-3 FFT dumps. Open PHY firmware = Tier 5.
notes: AR9271 is a single-chip USB 1x1 2.4GHz 11n SoC (Magpie). AR7010 is a USB/PCIe bridge (K2) that fronts an AR9280 or AR9287 radio. v2/v3 of the TL-WN722N use RTL8188EUS and are NOT this chip. Arbitrary-waveform is firmware-patch level (reported via modwifi), not a stock front-end IQ path.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC, driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 2x2 dual-band 11n SoftMAC. First generation with the spectral-scan FFT interface (Tier 3) and per-subcarrier CSI via the Atheros-CSI-Tool (Tier 2), all without firmware modification.
notes: Also used as the radio behind the AR7010 USB bridge in ath9k_htc dongles.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC, driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 1x1 2.4GHz 11n SoftMAC; spectral scan (Tier 3) and single-stream CSI (Tier 2) both work through the open driver / CSI Tool.
notes: Single spatial stream limits CSI to one RX chain, but amplitude+phase per subcarrier is still exposed.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC, driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 2x2 2.4GHz 11n SoftMAC; 2-stream CSI (Tier 2) plus spectral FFT (Tier 3). Also serves as the radio behind an AR7010 USB bridge.
notes: The 2.4GHz-only sibling of AR9280.

firmware.arch: ath9k SoftMAC (PHY logic in open driver, no separate blob)

sdr_tier_rationale: Uncompressed per-subcarrier CSI (56@20/114@40) via ath9k driver hook (Tier 2); same silicon also dumps raw FFT bins via spectral_scan (Tier 3).
notes: Full-precision CSI on the open ath9k stack; runs on PCs, embedded boards, and OpenWRT routers. See ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md.

firmware.arch: MIPS 74Kc SoC (host CPU) + ath9k PHY

notes: 2x2 802.11n router SoC validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors via the OpenWRT build path; yields per-packet CSI (Tier 2) and mainline ath9k spectral scan (Tier 3). Runs the modified ath9k on-device under OpenWRT — attractive for standalone/battery CSI sensing nodes rather than a host PC.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband), driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: The AR9003 / QCA9300 family is the most flexible receiver in the ath9k line. PicoScenes drives it with arbitrary carrier-frequency tuning across the full 2.4GHz span, 2.5-80 MHz baseband sampling, and 0-66 dB manual Rx gain, plus full CSI and spectral FFT. Not a raw-IQ streamer, so capped at Tier 3, but the raw-iq flag reflects the near-arbitrary tunable-receiver behaviour PicoScenes exposes (reported).
notes: AR9380 = 3x3, AR9382 = 2x2, AR9390 = integrated variant. Marketed as QCA9300 post-acquisition. raw-iq is PicoScenes-reported flexibility, not a stock ath9k feature.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband); BT coex block separate

sdr_reason: 2x2 dual-band 11n + Bluetooth combo on the ar9003 baseband; Wi-Fi side gives spectral FFT (Tier 3) and CSI (Tier 2) via the open driver and CSI Tool.
notes: Extremely common OEM laptop card (AR5B22). BT combo does not affect the Wi-Fi PHY telemetry paths.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband), driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: Low-cost 1x1 2.4GHz ar9003 part; still exposes spectral FFT (Tier 3) and single-stream CSI (Tier 2) through the open driver.
notes: Cheapest entry into the AR9003 CSI/spectral capability.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband), driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 3x3 dual-band ar9003 desktop/router PCIe part; one of the explicitly tested Atheros-CSI-Tool targets. 3-stream CSI (Tier 2) and spectral FFT (Tier 3), no firmware mod.
notes: Atheros-CSI-Tool was validated on AR9580, AR9590, AR9344, QCA9558. Three RX chains give the richest CSI in the 11n line.

firmware.arch: none (host-driven MAC/PHY via ath9k)

notes: 3x3 802.11n PCIe PHY explicitly validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors for per-packet CSI extraction; also exposes the mainline ath9k spectral-scan debugfs interface (Tier 3, 56/128-bin FFT). No firmware patch needed — the driver drives the PHY directly. Sibling to AR9380/AR9580.

firmware.arch: MIPS 74Kc SoC (host CPU) + ath9k PHY

notes: 3x3 802.11n SoC explicitly validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors (OpenWRT path); delivers 3x3 per-packet CSI (Tier 2) and ath9k spectral scan (Tier 3) with no firmware patch. On-device modified ath9k makes it a self-contained CSI sensing router.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa (on-chip), closed firmware blob loaded by ath10k

sdr_reason: 802.11ac wave-1. ath10k exposes the baseband spectral-scan FFT (spectral_bins 64/128/256) via debugfs — Tier 3. But the closed Xtensa firmware blocks the CSI path and constrains injection, so it sits below the ath9k parts despite newer silicon.
notes: Moving to 11ac introduced a closed on-chip firmware (unlike SoftMAC ath9k). ath10k-ct is a patched binary firmware, not open source. CSI is not turnkey on ath10k.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa (on-chip), closed firmware blob loaded by ath10k

sdr_reason: 802.11ac wave-2 (up to 4x4 MU-MIMO). Same Tier-3 spectral-scan FFT path as QCA988x; QCA9984/QCA9888 needed a kernel fix to strip an 8-byte segment-index header from each sample. Closed firmware, no turnkey CSI.
notes: 80+80/160 MHz support means wider FFT captures. QCA9888 is the 2x2 sibling.

firmware.arch: embedded Linux on quad ARC core cluster

notes: Runs embedded Linux internally on ARC cores; Quantenna publicly marketed Wi-Fi Sensing/CSI on these parts, making a documented CSI path plausible (tier 2 reported). No packaged community toolchain.

firmware.arch: Ralink/MediaTek hardware MAC + closed ucode blob

notes: Dual-band (2.4/5 GHz) 2x2 802.11n USB part, the dual-band sibling of the RT5370/RT5372. Supported in-kernel by rt2800usb/rt2x00, giving clean monitor mode + frame injection with no out-of-tree DKMS build - the cheapest no-hassle dual-band injector. Stalls at tier 1: no public CSI or spectral path on Ralink/MediaTek legacy USB silicon. Cataloged because the Panda PAU09 is a very common recommendation and is a distinct chip from the 2.4-only PAU05/PAU06 (RT5372).

firmware.arch: Thin on-chip MAC ucode (near soft-MAC to host)

notes: Original BackTrack-era injection card. Mainline mac80211 driver = monitor+injection out of the box. 2.4GHz only, high TX power. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: Cheap ubiquitous 2.4GHz n monitor/injection default. aircrack-ng/rtl8188eus is the reference DKMS driver. TL-WN722N v2/v3 use this (v1 was Atheros).

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: Later cheap 2.4GHz n part; monitor via out-of-tree forks, injection partial/flaky vs 8188EUS.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: Very common 2.4GHz 802.11n dongle. Monitor works; injection quality depends on rtl8192cu vs rtl8xxxu driver.

firmware.arch: Arm Cortex-M4F (KM4, 200MHz) + Cortex-M0 (KM0, 20MHz), FreeRTOS SDK

notes: The SDR-interesting Realtek: dual-band Wi-Fi MCU with OFFICIAL Wi-Fi CSI API (per-subcarrier I/Q, amplitude+phase, active/passive modes). Open documented FreeRTOS SDK, Cortex-M4+M0. Cheap BW16 boards. Tier 2 / rung-2 CSI. Ameba CSI framework spans RTL8721Dx/8720E/8730E/8735C.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband (+BT)

notes: 2.4GHz n + Bluetooth combo. Station mode solid; monitor possible but injection weak/driver-dependent. Catalogued for completeness.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: 1x1 dual-band AC sibling of 8812AU; same unified aircrack-ng driver. Monitor+injection. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: THE standard dual-band 2x2 AC injection dongle. Alfa AWUS036ACH. aircrack-ng/rtl8812au is the reference driver. Tier 1, no CSI/spectral.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: 'B' gen 2x2 AC (8822BU = +BT combo). Monitor solid; injection partial/less reliable than 8812AU — morrownr steers pentesters back to 8812AU/8821CU.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: 4x4 MIMO flagship (Alfa AWUS1900). Highest antenna count of Realtek line but still Tier 1. Dedicated rtl8814au fork adds AP+jammer; some distro rtl88xxau packages dropped 8814 support.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: 1x1 AC (AU-series) covered by the unified aircrack-ng/rtl8812au driver. Monitor+injection. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: 8051-class MCU + HW MAC/baseband

notes: Single-stream dual-band AC; morrownr's recommended cheap/small injection adapter. Clean monitor+injection. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: Realtek DVB-T demodulator ASIC (fixed function)

notes: RX-only 8-bit, ~0.5kHz-1.7GHz, ~2.4MHz BW. The genuine-SDR floor and the accidental-SDR archetype; see rtl-sdr-lineage.md. Listed tier 5 as reference datum only. Discovery: Eric Fry (2010) & Antti Palosaari (2012).

firmware.arch: Mirics tuner + FPGA/USB controller (closed)

notes: RX-only 14-bit, 1kHz-2GHz, up to 10MHz BW. Serious-listener receive tier.

firmware.arch: fixed-function LoRa/FSK transceiver (SPI-driven, no MCU)

notes: LoRa (chirp spread spectrum) plus full (G)FSK/OOK legacy mode. Continuous FSK/OOK mode streams an arbitrary bitstream (tones, jamming, replay); the LoRa engine gives CSS TX/RX directly. The LoRa PHY was reverse-engineered on real SDRs (gr-lora by Bastille/Matt Knight and by rpp0), a good example of using an SDR to crack a closed PHY these chips then speak natively. SX1280 is 2.4 GHz LoRa.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M3 (NRC7292)

notes: Industry-first IEEE 802.11ah Wi-Fi module, built on Newracom NRC7292. Range up to ~1.5 km; EVK targets Raspberry Pi. Inherits NRC7292 open GPL mac80211 driver (tier-1 monitor+injection) and closed radio firmware. Net-new named module record.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M4/M33 + radio driven by RAIL library

notes: RAIL (Radio Abstraction Interface Layer) exposes an arbitrary proprietary-PHY builder (custom modulation, symbol rate, framing), plus energy/RSSI scanning and TX tone/stream mode. Radio internals closed but RAIL documented (partially-documented). Tier 1 with a path to custom PHYs.

firmware.arch: fixed-function sub-GHz transceiver (SPI-driven, no MCU)

notes: 300-348/387-464/779-928 MHz, 2-FSK/GFSK/4-FSK/MSK/ASK/OOK. Async/sync serial transparent mode keys the PA directly from an arbitrary GPIO bit pattern, allowing verbatim replay of captured OOK/FSK waveforms (approaching arbitrary-waveform for simple modulations). The radio in the Flipper Zero. Fully documented PHY.

firmware.arch: Cortex-M3/M4 app core + dedicated Cortex-M0 RF Core with patchable ROM (RF patches)

notes: Two-core: Cortex-M3/M4 app + dedicated Cortex-M0 RF Core running the radio from a patchable ROM (RF patches). RF Core proprietary mode allows custom sub-GHz/2.4 GHz PHYs (arbitrary FSK/OOK params, packet formats); RSSI/CCA gives coarse spectrum sensing, reaching toward tier 3. driverlib open, RF ROM closed but patchable.

firmware.arch: fixed-function 2.4 GHz transceiver (SPI-driven, no MCU)

notes: 2.4 GHz sibling of CC1101 (GFSK/OOK/MSK) with the same transparent-mode raw-bitstream replay trick. The radio in many 2.4 GHz RC and peripheral links. Tier 1, documented PHY.

firmware.arch: 8051 core + 2.4 GHz radio

notes: CC2531 = 802.15.4/Zigbee USB sniffer; CC2540 = BLE sniffer. Stock sniffer firmware from TI, plus community whsniff+Wireshark (CC2531) and ZBOSS zboss_sniffer.hex. Tier 1 monitor within their standards; injection with custom firmware.

firmware.arch: Arm Cort-R4F + C674x DSP (mmWave SDK)

notes: PURPOSE-BUILT radar included as the yardstick, NOT a repurposed Wi-Fi chip. Single-chip FMCW radar: IWR6843 at 60-64 GHz (industrial/IoT), AWR1642/AWR6843 at 76-81 GHz (automotive, band outside this catalog's enum). Full control of the chirp waveform (start freq/slope/ramp) and raw ADC IQ streamed off-chip via DCA1000EVM into mmWave Studio, then range-FFT -> Doppler-FFT -> angle-FFT. Delivers true range-Doppler-angle imaging with ~cm range bins -- tier 4 natively (arbitrary FMCW + raw IQ), documented PHY. This is what the beam-SNR Wi-Fi approach is measured against.

firmware.arch: TI proprietary WiLink MAC/PHY controller

notes: Open mac80211 driver stack (wlcore+wl18xx+wlcore_sdio) gives monitor mode and radiotap injection. Firmware is a closed blob from git.ti.com; no CSI/PHY-telemetry path and no public patching toolchain, so the ladder stops at tier 1.

firmware.arch: Synopsys ARC (ARCompact) WiGig firmware; MIPS/ARM host running LEDE/OpenWrt

notes: The workhorse of practically all 60 GHz Wi-Fi sensing research: 32-element planar phased array, single 60 GHz stream. Teardowns show Sparrow QCA6320+QCA6310 silicon; sensing papers commonly write 'QCA9500 transceiver' for the same wil6210/ARC family. SEEMOO's LEDE port gives root + custom firmware loading; nexmon-arc's sweep_dump exposes per-sector beam-SNR at /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/wil6210/sweep_dump. Used for device-free localization, gesture recognition, and short-range SAR imaging via aperture motion. Distinct from the already-cataloged qualcomm-qca9500 chip record.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Zynq-7045 (ZC706) / Zynq-7020 (ZedBoard) / Zynq UltraScale+ (ZCU102) FPGA baseband in Verilog + Linux mac80211 driver

common_hardware: Xilinx ZC706 / ZedBoard / ZCU102 dev board
notes: Reference dev-board path for openwifi: a Xilinx evaluation board (ZC706 Zynq-7045, ZedBoard Zynq-7020, or ZCU102 UltraScale+) plus an AD-FMCOMMS2/3/4 (AD9361) FMC RF card. Larger PL (ZC706/ZCU102) hosts the full 2x2 build; ZC706/ZCU102 need a paid Vivado licence, ZedBoard is WebPACK-buildable.
